articles.title: Home Assistant asks before sharing phone data with another home
articles.dek: Adding another server requires explicit choices for location and sensor sharing before those readings are sent.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple app asks what a second or later server may receive before sharing the device’s location and sensors. Previously, adding another server silently selected precise location and all sensors, including readings enabled for a different home.

The new setup step starts with neither choice selected and requires an answer to both. Sensor data stays back until the person decides; abandoning setup leaves the new server sending nothing until its settings are changed.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves also stops setup from silently treating the current Wi-Fi network as the server’s home network. A network must be shown and confirmed before it is saved. Existing saved networks remain in place and can be removed from the server’s Internal URL settings.

pullRequests.title: Ask for privacy choices when adding another server
Ask before using a Wi-Fi network as a server's home network

articles.title: Threema gains Home Assistant notifications with optional end-to-end encryption
articles.dek: The new integration sends text to configured recipients through Threema Gateway.
body: Home Assistant automations gain a route to send text messages through Threema Gateway. Each configured recipient gets a notification entity, giving households a dedicated destination for alerts.

Setup accepts an existing Gateway ID and secret and can generate an encryption key pair. Providing a private key enables end-to-end mode; leaving it empty uses the gateway’s non-end-to-end mode. Threema must enable end-to-end mode for the gateway after its public key is registered.
Lukas makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the integration, which starts with outgoing text messages.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps repeated spoken messages from falling silent
articles.dek: Cached speech could play once, then fail on ESPHome and other strict audio decoders.
body: A spoken Home Assistant message could work the first time and become silent when repeated later. The correction prevents duplicate audio metadata from making the saved copy unreadable to stricter players, including an ESPHome media player used to verify the problem.

The first request plays an in-memory copy, while a later request can use the saved file after that cache expires. Bryce Boe corrects how the file’s existing metadata is updated. Chromecast players tolerate the duplicate metadata and are unaffected by this failure.

pullRequests.title: Fix duplicate ID3 tag when tagging TTS audio

articles.title: Home Assistant stops dense history timelines freezing the interface
articles.dek: Long runs of tiny state changes are fitted to the chart’s visible width.
body: Opening a Home Assistant history timeline with tens of thousands of state changes could freeze the interface for seconds. Petar Petrov limits the amount drawn to the chart’s device-pixel width instead of laying out a separate rectangle for every change.

State periods wide enough to show keep their exact boundaries. Shorter changes share a screen-sized slice represented by the state occupying most of it, keeping dense histories readable without drawing invisible detail.

pullRequests.title: Downsample the history timeline to the chart's pixel width

articles.title: Theben Conexa meters bring energy totals into Home Assistant locally
articles.dek: The new integration reads consumed and supplied energy from the smart-meter gateway.
body: Households with a Theben Conexa smart-meter gateway gain local Home Assistant readings for cumulative energy consumed and supplied. The integration polls the gateway directly and creates sensors for the totals it provides.

Setup needs the gateway address and credentials supplied by the power-grid operator, and the gateway must already be reachable through a browser. Michael Dluhosch makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the integration.

pullRequests.title: Add a new integration for Theben Conexa smartmeter gateway

articles.title: Home Assistant withdraws its new Apple Watch energy panel
articles.dek: The watch-face addition reported on September 20 has been removed from the app’s development code.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple app withdraws the daily-energy watch-face panel described in the September 20 edition of OHF Daily. Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves reverses the development addition, which combined daily energy figures with a compact chart for each connected home.

articles.title: Home Assistant switches Bosch’s presence simulation on and off
articles.dek: The controller’s away-from-home routine gains a control alongside its existing devices.
body: Bosch Smart Home households gain a Home Assistant switch for the controller’s presence simulation. It turns the existing routine on or off, letting automations control the feature intended to make an empty home appear occupied. Thomas exposes the controller’s existing capability; Home Assistant does not create its own simulation.

pullRequests.title: bosch_shc: add presence simulation switch entity

articles.title: Music Assistant restores artist recommendations for restricted accounts
articles.dek: Shared metadata remains visible even when a listener cannot access every music source.
body: Music Assistant restores similar artists and top tracks supplied by shared metadata services such as Last.fm for listeners with restricted music-source access. Opening an artist page could show a false permission error, while the default view silently left those recommendations out.
Marcel van der Veldt keeps the restrictions on music sources while allowing household-wide metadata providers through.

pullRequests.title: Fix false permission error opening an artist page

articles.title: Matter.js Server adds room selection for compatible robot vacuums
articles.dek: Its own dashboard can select areas, skip queued rooms and show cleaning progress when the device supports those controls.
body: Matter.js Server’s own dashboard gains room and area selection for compatible robot vacuums. It keeps the device’s current selection checked when someone changes the cleaning plan, and offers a Skip control for queued or active areas when the device supports it.

Ludovic BOUÉ also adds reported progress and estimated completion times. Ingo Fischer reviewed the panel; testing with a physical vacuum remains outstanding. These controls apply to Matter.js Server’s dashboard.

pullRequests.title: Adds dashboard command support for the Matter Service Area cluster

articles.title: Monarch Money reconnects without rebuilding its Home Assistant integration
articles.dek: An expired login can be renewed while preserving existing devices and entities.
body: Home Assistant lets Monarch Money users sign back in when their token expires instead of deleting and recreating the integration. The recovery flow supports multifactor authentication and checks that the same account is being reconnected.
Temporary connection failures continue to retry without demanding another login. Bradley Florence also enables saved-credential autofill for the email and password fields.

pullRequests.title: Enable credential autofill for Monarch Money

articles.title: ESPHome stops pairing components that cannot work together
articles.dek: Device Builder filters incompatible choices before they become configuration errors.
body: ESPHome Device Builder stops offering known-incompatible connections when a maker adds a component. A single-color dimmable light no longer offers an on/off-only output, and adding a Hörmann cover creates the kind of Modbus connection it needs instead of choosing one that configuration checks reject.

J. Nick Koston applies the matching to the visual picker, configuration suggestions and automatically selected dependencies. Choices stay available when the builder lacks enough information to judge them, including configurations assembled from other files.
